message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 121, "amount_cents": 3797}, {"order_id": 122, "amount_cents": 5470}, {"order_id": 124, "amount_cents": 1085}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order list to see which customers are affected and confirm the handoff's refund claims against the ledger.
The handoff claims three refunds, and they map to the birch and cobalt orders. I'll check the refund ledger to confirm they were actually applied before computing any payouts.

The refund ledger matches the handoff exactly, so the three refunds are confirmed. The customers in the batch are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 31368 matches its order total (5706 + 25662) with no refunds, so it checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect refunds 121 and 124.

Birch's net balance of 16201 matches its orders (8002 + 13081 = 21083) minus refunds 121 and 124 (3797 + 1085 = 4882), so it checks out. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance, which should reflect refund 122.

Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194 = 29756) minus refund 122 (5470). All three balances reconcile with the orders and refund ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 31368 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 16201, which matches its reconciled net balance.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net balance of 24286 reconciled against its orders and refund 122. I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each matched its order total minus refunds from the ledger, so the batch is complete.
